findings.title: Non-root container is denied a path in its image
findings.cause: container web runs as user 1000 and is denied /www, a path of the image itself, not of a volume: the image's files belong to root, and another user may not create or change them; its log says: "mkdir: can't create directory '/www': Permission denied"; Deployment web has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container web exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container web's log (run that exited)
evidence.detail: mkdir: can't create directory '/www': Permission denied

evidence.what: container web runs as user 1000 (runAsUser), and /www is not under any of its volume mounts
evidence.command: kubectl get pod web-8cbd88466-7tdh4 -n kd-nonroot-writes-image-path -o jsonpath='{.spec.securityContext}{" "}{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="web")].securityContext}{" "}{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="web")].volumeMounts[*].mountPath}'

findings.fix: Give the app a place it may write: mount an emptyDir at /www (or its parent directory) and set the pod's fsGroup, or point the app at a writable directory such as /tmp. Or build the image so that /www belongs to the user it runs as.
